Omar: Heads-up, found a quirky repro: Rollup + terser (via Vite) minify + SDK default export -> Edge runtime crash.
Val: what error?
Omar: On deploy to Vercel Edge: `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`. Local Node (dev mode) works fine.
Rina: classic default vs named? or mangled class name from minifier?
Omar: Turns out it's both. Minimal repro steps I used:
```
# clone
git clone https://example.com/rw-bundle-mangle-repro.git
cd rw-bundle-mangle-repro
npm ci
# build using vite (production with esbuild/terser mix)
npm run build
# inspect dist/vendor.js and run in node --input-type=module or deploy to edge
node --input-type=module dist/server.js
```
Omar: App code is tiny:
```
import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
await client.generate('hello');
```
Omar: In the bundle vendor chunk the SDK shows up as an interop object, and terser mangles the constructor name (class) when `keep_fnames` not enabled. On Edge this becomes unconstructable.
Val: Do you have the vendor snippet?
Omar: yes, trimmed: `var g=(()=>{function n(){}return n})();export default g;` after minify. Then runtime tries `new g()` but because interop wrapper re-exports weirdly it fails.
Rina: Interesting. Also some bundlers replace `require()` shims and remove interop helpers for ESM-only targets which can exacerbate this. Which minifier did Vite use? esbuild or terser?
Omar: On this project Vite config uses terser for css + esbuild for JS in earlier versions, but we hit a plugin that switched to terser for JS mangle in CI. The culprit seems to be terser removing the class name and the interop layer expecting it. Edge stricter resolution + conditional exports caused rollup to pick a different entry in some runs.
Val: Workarounds I tested: 1) set terserOptions: { keep_fnames: true } or esbuild minify with keepNames. 2) change SDK consumption to `import * as RW from 'redwood-inference'; const Client = RW.default ?? RW;` 3) prefer named `createClient` export in SDK.
Omar: Yep. Also when bundler resolves to CJS path (`dist/index.cjs`) then it pulls in a CommonJS wrapper that relies on `module.exports.default` interop which Edge won't provide; that sometimes manifests as the same constructor error.
Rina: Actionable fixes:
- SDK: publish a named ESM export `export function createClient(opts){ return new RedwoodClient(opts) }` and update README recommending `import { createClient }` for edge apps.
- SDK: add `exports.browser` conditional pointing to `dist/index.browser.mjs` so bundlers targeting browsers/edges pick a stable ESM build.
- Consumers: set minifier to preserve function/class names (`keep_fnames` / `keepNames`) as short-term workaround.
- Tooling: add CI bundle-smoke tests that build with vite/rollup/webpack + minify and run resulting bundle in `node --input-type=module` to catch these before release.

Omar: I already opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/489 with repro repo + vendor chunk + build logs. Assigned to @pkg-maintainers.
Val: Also add a tiny example in `examples/edge/` that uses Vite config with recommended terser/options so onboarding customers don't hit this.
Rina: Good call. I'll add the CI job for bundle-smoke tests and a checklist for packaging changes.
DevOps-bot: CI job bundle-check failed on branch fix/keep-names: `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor` (see https://ci.example.com/build/314159).
Omar: Thanks team 44aa I'll attach the failing bundle + suggested terser config in the issue. Will follow up when PR is ready.
